_comment: Generation Loss is a faithful client-side reproduction of the recursive-resampling model behind language-model collapse: each generation draws a finite sample of size M from the current distribution and refits the next distribution from it. This file holds the model parameters and the documented anchor figures shown in the readout/caption. The animation generates no empirical numbers of its own — it re-runs a documented mechanism.

presets.label: small batch
presets.note: A thin sample per generation — the tails starve fast and the support collapses within a handful of generations.

presets.label: web-scale
presets.note: More samples slow the drift, but replace still wanders away from the original and concentrates.

presets.label: huge batch
presets.note: Even a huge per-generation sample only buys time: replace collapses eventually; the bound is finite only under accumulate.

anchors.shumailov_model: OPT-125m fine-tuned recursively on its own generations (wikitext2): perplexity climbs every generation and output degenerates to repetitive text by generation 9.
anchors.early_vs_late: Early collapse loses the tails (rare events) first; late collapse converges to a point estimate with little variance.
anchors.gaussian_certainty: In the tractable 1D Gaussian model, finite-sample refitting makes collapse certain: the variance is absorbed at zero as generations grow.
anchors.accumulate_bound: Replacing data each generation makes test error diverge with the iteration count; accumulating real + synthetic data caps it at a finite upper bound independent of the number of iterations.
anchors.c2pa: C2PA content credentials prove who signed a manifest and when — signing, not truth. A valid credential does not establish that the bytes are human-authored or uncontaminated.

sources.label: Shumailov et al., 'AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data', Nature 2024
Gerstgrasser et al., 'Is Model Collapse Inevitable? Breaking the Curse of Recursion by Accumulating Real and Synthetic Data', 2024
